blocks.x: Cyber Resilience & Incident Recovery, delivered by a named pod: the scope, the rhythm, the rails, and the numbers we are willing to be measured on.

Resilience is a delivery capability, not a document: tested recovery for crown-jewel systems, immutable backups with restored-and-verified proof, segregation of the recovery environment from the compromised estate, and a rehearsed crisis playbook with named decision roles. We build the technical program — BCP/DR alignment to business RTO/RPO, clean-room recovery architecture, ransomware-specific playbooks — and run the exercises that make it real: tabletop for leadership, technical fire drills for teams.

We also harden the boring failure paths: third-party and supply-chain risk with SBOM tracking, email-borne compromise chains, and insider-risk controls calibrated to culture. Post-incident, we run blameless reviews that convert events into backlog items with owners and dates — the metric is time-to-recovery, and it is measured every exercise.

Delivery runs on one weekly rhythm for every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline with your team: the current metric is measured, signed and stored as the reference for every later gate. Weeks 3–8 run the pilot on deliberately narrow scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, never quietly extended.
